clue.text: Channel No 7, say?

blocks.note: the seventh letter of the alphabet
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A query about whether a perfume like Chanel No 5 has a sister scent, No 7.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Chanel No 5 perfume, but 'No 7' here simply means letter number seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel along a roof edge or road for carrying away rainwater.

clue.text: A crammed grid maybe bringing pleasure?

definitions.note: archaic sense of the answer: pleasing, agreeable

indicators.note: maybe flags that the phrase is only approximately the answer, matching it by its spoken sound

blocks.note: a grid such as a fireplace grate, crammed full

explanation.surface: Asking whether filling a crossword grid to bursting gives satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'grid' is not a crossword but a fire grate; a stuffed one is a 'grate full'.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense the word means pleasing to the senses, agreeable, as in 'a grateful shade'.

clue.text: With conspiracy theorist as hostage, five times he has lost it

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander out of order
a hostage is held captive, so the series of letters holds the other parts inside it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time, taken five times
the anagram fodder
David Icke, former TV sports presenter turned conspiracy theorist

explanation.surface: A conspiracy theorist is held hostage, and he has repeatedly lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The five T's are spaced out with the rearranged HE HAS and ICKE filling the gaps. 'Lost it' looks like an idiom, but 'it' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That's the ticket!' and 'That's it!' both exclaim that something is exactly what is wanted.

clue.text: Macmillan, Cameron and Johnson out of it; Truss wouldn't wear it

definitions.text: Macmillan, Cameron and Johnson out of it

blocks.clueFragment: Macmillan, Cameron and Johnson out of it
blocks.note: first meaning: a ... or batch produced by the famous school, as all three Prime Ministers were
second meaning: a short boyish women's hairstyle of the 1920s

explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss, unlike those three Prime Ministers, did not go to Eton, and with her longer hair would not sport the 1920s cut either.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a short, sleek women's haircut and, punningly, a harvest of old boys from the school.

clue.text: Pushy type, Oscar, gets slightly pushier, putting one out

indicators.note: first half of 'putting ... out': to put something out is to eject it
completes 'putting ... out', so the numeral for one is ejected from the phrase

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
'a bit ruder': slightly more impertinent
Roman numeral one, removed

explanation.surface: A forward person gets a little more forward, elbowing someone aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of BIT RUDER to leave BTRUDER, then put O in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An obtruder thrusts himself or his opinions forward uninvited, so is a pushy sort of person.

clue.text: With recoil, show contempt for compiler on the prowl

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining a participle: recoiling

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer in contempt
the setter refers to himself
roaming about in search of prey

explanation.surface: Jeering at a crossword setter who is out hunting, only for it to come back at you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' is the crossword setter, who in wordplay is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boomeranging is rebounding on its originator, flying back like the Australian throwing stick, so it recoils.

clue.text: Separate reserves call for the receiver

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to set aside funds

blocks.note: to ring is to telephone, to call
a fence receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A request that someone on the phone pick up the handset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a telephone handset; it is the criminal dealer in stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to guarantee it is kept apart for one purpose, protecting it as separate reserves.

clue.text: One nub followed by another perhaps more reason than usual to get a 22

definitions.text: One nub followed by another perhaps
more reason than usual to get a 22

blocks.clueFragment: One nub followed by another perhaps
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: NUB NUB is two buns, i.e. two rolls, written backwards

blocks.clueFragment: more reason than usual to get a 22
blocks.note: second meaning: a lottery jackpot carried over twice, a strong incentive to buy a ticket (the answer at 22)

explanation.walkthrough: Reversed, NUB reads BUN, a roll; two of them reversed is a double roll over. 22 refers to TICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: When a lottery jackpot is unwon twice in a row it rolls over twice, swelling the prize and the urge to buy in.

clue.text: Divers aren't carrying a woman

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or assorted, so these letters come in a different arrangement
carrying something means holding it within, so the jumble holds the article

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scuba divers are not giving a lady a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the plural of diver; here it is the archaic adjective meaning sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Renata is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: One vigorous woman for each chap with cross to bear!

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it, so the chap holds the cross inside him

blocks.note: as in 'a pound a head', a means per or for each
a chap is a man
a zo (or dzo) is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A sturdy woman is paired with every man who has a burden to shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: ZO, a Himalayan yak-cow hybrid, is a favourite crossword animal; 'cross' looks like a crucifix or anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a legendary race of warrior women, so an amazon is any strong, forceful woman.

clue.text: Decline bank issue

blocks.note: a down is a bank of sand or a rolling hill
a turn is an outcome, as in a turn of events

explanation.surface: A bank's share issue, or its banknotes, falling in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank issue' reads as money a bank puts out; split it into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in economic activity or prices, the same as a decline.

clue.text: With crestfallen brass in house lies new couple

indicators.note: in a down entry the crest, the top letter, falls to the bottom
in places the money inside the abbreviation for house

blocks.note: brass is slang for money
HO is the abbreviation for house
a oner, in Chambers, is a big lie or whopper

explanation.surface: Dejected senior officers in the Commons are telling falsehoods, along with a recently formed pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' suggests senior officers and 'house' Parliament; ONER as a whopper is a dictionary sense many solvers won't know.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeymooners are a newly married pair on their first holiday together, so a new couple.

clue.text: Quartet's second offering creates upset, it's fair to admit

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, its letters thrown into disorder
to admit is to let in, so the second part goes inside the first

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
saying something is fair means it is OK

explanation.surface: A string quartet's second piece causes upset, it must be admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The quartet is literary, not musical: T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets, whose second poem is named after a Somerset village.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is the second of the four poems making up Eliot's Four Quartets.

clue.text: See 12
At security door of your apartment, don't forget this excitement!

blocks.note: an apartment; 'of' makes it possessive
a keypad door lock asks for a personal identification number

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget your code when you reach the secure entrance, alarm and all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole as 'the flat's PIN' — the number you must remember at its security door.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flat spin is to be in a state of agitated panic, so it names excited confusion.

clue.text: Doctor put everyone on cut bananas

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
in a down entry, one part on another sits above it, so the parts follow in order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
to hew is to cut with an axe
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A medic prescribes sliced bananas for every patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit in the surface; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up the wall and going bananas are both informal idioms for becoming crazy or furious.

clue.text: See 6
Like e.g. 3 27, but not 31, having cut a dash?

blocks.note: first meaning: written as separate words with no linking marks, as the haircut at 3 and 27 is, unlike the entry at 31
second meaning: with the dash taken out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut a dash' is the idiom for looking stylish; here a dash is literally cut away. The answer at 31 is printed with two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A term written without hyphens is unhyphenated, which describes the two-word haircut but not the triple-part phrase at 31.

clue.text: See 7
Right to avoid the Spanish fleet coming up over southern water

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep out of it, so this letter is dropped
in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top
over here means wrapped around, so the reversed phrase covers the next letter

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right; it is removed
el is Spanish for the
an armada is a fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: The Armada sailing north past the south coast, steering clear of the right flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' sits at the end looking like part of the naval scene; it is the definition. The Spanish article and the fleet are joined before anything is removed or turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular name for water, the only drink available to the first man.

clue.text: Please kings with gifts, crowd buzzing

indicators.note: a buzzing crowd is milling about excitedly, so its letters move around

blocks.note: the Magi, the three kings who brought gifts to the infant Jesus
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A buzzing crowd entertains royal visitors bearing presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a verb meaning to delight; it is the polite word itself, which children are told is 'the magic word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are taught that 'please' is the magic word that gets them what they ask for.

clue.text: Continues without change on Circle but not Met Line

blocks.note: is in the sense of remains or exists unchanged
a circle is the shape of the letter O
bar means except, i.e. but not

explanation.surface: A London Underground note: the Circle line runs as normal, unlike the Metropolitan line.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle and Met are both London Underground lines, but 'Met' here is short for meteorological.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal pressure, so a meteorological line.

clue.text: See 2
See 14
Add to bubbling cauldron minute shellfish

indicators.note: the contents of a bubbling pot churn about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: put tiny shellfish into the simmering pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like the adjective for tiny; it is the time unit, abbreviated. 'Add to' tells you to put its letter in with the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The round clam, or quahog, is an edible North American bivalve, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: See 24
See 15
See 3
Knight, on way through plot, charged with tart theft?

indicators.note: something running through a plot of ground lies inside it

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for knight
the nave is the central passage or way through a church
a garden plot is a bed

explanation.surface: A knight on the road through a conspiracy stands accused of stealing pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the Knave of Hearts stole the tarts, so anyone accused of it has been called a knave.
explanation.definitionFit: To beknave someone is to call them a knave, which is what the thief of the Queen of Hearts' tarts was.

clue.text: What do you know about Appia, Dolorosa and Labicana?

definitions.text: What do you know about Appia, Dolorosa and Labicana?

blocks.clueFragment: What do you know about Appia, Dolorosa and Labicana?
blocks.note: surface reading: a quiz question about three obscure names
setter's reading: each is a Via, so the three together are a trio of Roman-style roads

explanation.walkthrough: Via Appia, Via Dolorosa and Via Labicana make three vias; the question format suggests a pub quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are unimportant facts of the kind tested in quizzes, exactly what a 'what do you know' question asks for.

clue.text: Brutal, like the post-1934 New York Yankees?

definitions.text: like the post-1934 New York Yankees

blocks.note: first meaning: merciless, without pity

blocks.clueFragment: like the post-1934 New York Yankees
blocks.note: second meaning: Babe Ruth played his last Yankees season in 1934, so the team afterwards was without Ruth

explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the New York Yankees' baseball legend; after he left in 1934 the team was literally Ruth-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ruthless shows no pity or compassion, which makes them cruel and brutal.

clue.text: Something unique in newspaper's editorial

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Something one-off appears in a paper's leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the clue is ignored; the letters run from inside the first word into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-per-se is a person or thing that is pre-eminent or unique, first of its kind as A is among letters.
